title: data-recorder-probes-report-to-the-watch
intention: Every standing WATCHME probe berthed in cairn/tools/data_recorder reports to harbor_master's watch verb with {ticket, holds, finding} stated against its own ticket's falsifier, and each spec names that receiver.
why: Every standing probe in cairn/tools/data_recorder mails with no verb and nothing uses it (835b5736bf2b D2); a88d6a368cfb built the watch verb that uses a WATCHME finding and 8ecb99998254 built watch_carry. Akien's answer to open-291189a9766a: build the receivers.
traces_to: 835b5736bf2b's falsifier (zero probe-bearing standing specs lack a receiver) and Akien's answer to open-291189a9766a; the 2026-09-30 ruling that a probe's data must have a consumer that USES it; RULE 1 (the build stays inside cairn/tools/data_recorder; base's helper through its public interface, harbor_master through its bus verb)
how: Measured 2026-10-03: 1 tickets at a rest carry a watchme probe under cairn/tools/data_recorder/probes/ (a4c2be029f49). Read 2026-10-03: one standing ticket (a4c2be029f49, at PROVED) carries a probe under cairn/tools/data_recorder/probes: declared_cadence_discriminates, posting to='harbor_master' with no verb and body ticket a4c2be029f49. Trigger: pop['read'] >= 1; enough: read >= 3 and >= 2 distinct declared frequencies. The spec's enough states the failure branch (the overdue troubles never discriminate, so the frequency is stripped) and is deliberately not time-bounded. census() in the beside module returns troubles keyed recorder-read-overdue-* and a current list. One proof imports it: cairn/tools/data_recorder/proofs/test_reading_declaration.py (asserts PROBE.body['ticket'] == 'a4c2be029f49', PROBE.to == 'harbor_master', carry and enough set; never the verb). Each PROBE gets verb='watch' and carry=watch_carry(<its id>, _carry, <its predicate>), importing watch_carry from cairn.tools.base.probe (declared public). Each ticket's watchme spec gains receiver {what: 'harbor_master watch verb', in: 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} through the artifact door. A proof under cairn/tools/data_recorder/proofs reads the population from the commons and asserts each probe's verb, to, and live payload invariants.
falsifier: GREEN when every ticket at PROVED or WATCHME whose watchme.probe sits under cairn/tools/data_recorder has a probe whose PROBE posts verb 'watch' to 'harbor_master' and whose payload over live data carries ticket == that ticket's id, holds a bool, and a non-empty finding whenever holds is False; and every such spec names receiver {what: 'harbor_master watch verb', in: 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} with watchme_spec_error naming no receiver fault. RED if any standing data_recorder spec lacks the receiver, or if a converted payload's ticket is a path or another id. WRONG INTENT if a data_recorder probe's data has a reader other than its own ticket's FIXME that only Akien could name.
watchme: none, because what this child's probes say is read by harbor_master's watch verb (a88d6a368cfb, PROVED), and whether they ever fire is 164da559823d's and acb4ecd84364's watch (CairnCommons/tickets/164da559823d-*.json); a probe on probes reporting would need a receiver of its own.
children: none, because the change is 1 PROBE declarations and their specs, all inside cairn/tools/data_recorder.
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Which probes and how: a4c2be029f49 declared_cadence_discriminates (holds=_holds). In each file under cairn/tools/data_recorder/probes/: append watch_carry to the existing 'from cairn.tools.base.probe import ...' line; use the probe's id constant (named per probe below, added as `_TICKET_ID = "<id>"` after the import block when absent); in PROBE = Probe(...) replace 'carry=_carry,' with 'verb="watch",' and 'carry=watch_carry(<const>, _carry, <pred>),'. declared_cadence_discriminates already holds TICKET = "a4c2be029f49" (the 12-hex id), which watch_carry takes as its ticket; no constant is added. Its trigger fires from the first read recorder and its enough is discriminates(pop) (three read recorders under two distinct frequencies), so before enough a post is growth, not a fault. The spec's enough names the failing closing: at enough, if the overdue troubles do not discriminate (every read-against recorder current), the WRONG INTENT clause is confirmed and the ticket is kicked so the frequency can be stripped. So it gains this holds predicate, inserted exactly as follows just above PROBE = Probe(: def _holds(context: dict) -> bool: ⏎     """Before ENOUGH a post is the population growing toward the bar, not a fault. At ENOUGH ⏎     the spec names two closings: the overdue judgement DISCRIMINATES (at least one read-against ⏎     recorder overdue and at least one current) and the watch closes green; or none is overdue, ⏎     the WRONG INTENT branch, and the ticket goes to FIXME, where the frequency is stripped. The ⏎     census is the at-rest probe's own pure judgement at this beat's clock (835b5736bf2b child).""" ⏎     from cairn.tools.data_recorder.probes.reading_is_declared_and_current import OVERDUE, census ⏎     pop = once(context, "recorder_population", lambda: population()) ⏎     if not discriminates(pop): ⏎         return True ⏎     c = census(datetime.now(timezone.utc)) ⏎     overdue = sum(1 for identity in c["troubles"] if identity.startswith(OVERDUE)) ⏎     return overdue >= 1 and len(c["current"]) >= 1 ; and passes carry=watch_carry(TICKET, _carry, holds=_holds). The local import is deliberate: it keeps the module-level import line unchanged (the at-rest module already imports nothing from this one, so there is no cycle either way). The second probe file in the folder, reading_is_declared_and_current.py, is no ticket's watchme probe (grep 2026-10-03), so it is not standing and is not converted. Nothing else in a probe changes. (2) watch_carry exists in cairn/tools/base/probe.py (8ecb99998254); do not edit it. (3) Specs: each ticket's watchme spec whose probe starts with cairn/tools/data_recorder/probes/ gains receiver {what: 'harbor_master watch verb', in: 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'}, through cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write. (4) Proof: cairn/tools/data_recorder/proofs/test_data_recorder_probes_report_to_the_watch.py, PROVES {'39c8d14a459f': {'all': 'test_data_recorder_probes_report_to_the_watch'}}, modeled on cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch.py. (5) Every proof that imports a converted probe stays green: run them.

Its trigger fires from the first read recorder and its enough is discriminates(pop) (three read recorders under two distinct frequencies), so before enough a post is growth, not a fault. The spec's enough names the failing closing: at enough, if the overdue troubles do not discriminate (every read-against recorder current), the WRONG INTENT clause is confirmed and the ticket is kicked so the frequency can be stripped. So it gains this holds predicate, inserted exactly as follows just above PROBE = Probe(: def _holds(context: dict) -> bool: ⏎     """Before ENOUGH a post is the population growing toward the bar, not a fault. At ENOUGH ⏎     the spec names two closings: the overdue judgement DISCRIMINATES (at least one read-against ⏎     recorder overdue and at least one current) and the watch closes green; or none is overdue, ⏎     the WRONG INTENT branch, and the ticket goes to FIXME, where the frequency is stripped. The ⏎     census is the at-rest probe's own pure judgement at this beat's clock (835b5736bf2b child).""" ⏎     from cairn.tools.data_recorder.probes.reading_is_declared_and_current import OVERDUE, census ⏎     pop = once(context, "recorder_population", lambda: population()) ⏎     if not discriminates(pop): ⏎         return True ⏎     c = census(datetime.now(timezone.utc)) ⏎     overdue = sum(1 for identity in c["troubles"] if identity.startswith(OVERDUE)) ⏎     return overdue >= 1 and len(c["current"]) >= 1 ; and passes carry=watch_carry(TICKET, _carry, holds=_holds). The second probe file in the folder, reading_is_declared_and_current.py, is no ticket's watchme probe (grep 2026-10-03), so it is not standing and is not converted. watch_carry's signature (cairn/tools/base/probe.py): watch_carry(ticket_id: str, carry=None, *, fails=None, holds=None), exactly one of fails=/holds= given as a keyword. <its predicate> is the literal keyword argument named in the parentheses above for that file: `fails=_trigger` passes the probe's existing module-level `_trigger` function (the same one already given to Probe as trigger=), and needs no new function. `holds=_holds` passes a `_holds` function defined as stated in this decision. Each named file exists (read 2026-10-03) with a `from cairn.tools.base.probe import ...` line and a `PROBE = Probe(...)` call holding `carry=_carry,`. Nothing else changes; watch_carry is not edited.

D2: the proof — Create cairn/tools/data_recorder/proofs/test_data_recorder_probes_report_to_the_watch.py by copying the existing file cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch.py (sealed green under 8d3c36e1fe59) byte for byte and then making ONLY these modifications: with the docstring naming cairn/tools/data_recorder and ticket 39c8d14a459f; PROVES = {'39c8d14a459f': {'all': 'test_data_recorder_probes_report_to_the_watch'}}; BERTH = 'cairn/tools/data_recorder/probes/'; _REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] (the repo root: the directory holding cairn/); teeth renamed test_every_standing_data_recorder_probe_posts_watch, test_every_standing_data_recorder_spec_names_the_receiver and the composite test_data_recorder_probes_report_to_the_watch. Structure, in full: imports importlib, json, subprocess, sys, Path; _REPO_ROOT on sys.path; parse_workflow from cairn.tools.base.transitions; watchme_spec_error from cairn.tools.base.watchme_spec; _main_tree() = Path(git -C _REPO_ROOT rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir).parent falling back to _REPO_ROOT; _tickets() = _main_tree().parent/'CairnCommons'/'tickets'; _standing() = (id, doc, spec) for each ticket whose parse_workflow(doc['workflow_and_state']).here is 'PROVED' or 'WATCHME' (a ticket that does not parse is skipped) whose watchme spec's probe starts with BERTH (every such spec: a ticket whose watchme is a list may contribute more than one tuple, and _specs() reads a dict or a list of dicts), asserting non-empty with `assert out, ...`; the posts tooth imports each probe module, takes payload = PROBE.payload({}) (Probe.payload runs the carry over that context), and asserts PROBE.verb == 'watch', PROBE.to == 'harbor_master', payload({}) carries ticket == the id, holds a bool, non-empty finding when holds is False (invariants only); the receiver tooth asserts spec['receiver'] == {'what': 'harbor_master watch verb', 'in': 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} and watchme_spec_error(doc) names no receiver fault; a __main__ block runs each, prints PASS/FAIL, exits 1 on any failure. No classes.

D3: the specs' receiver — Write one Python script file (in the session scratchpad) that does the following, and run it. Ticket files are /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/tickets/<id>-<slug>.json (glob '<id>-*.json', exactly one). For each of a4c2be029f49: doc = json.loads(Path(p).read_text()); the watchme is a dict or list of dicts; every spec whose 'probe' starts with 'cairn/tools/data_recorder/probes/' (one or several) gets spec['receiver'] = {'what': 'harbor_master watch verb', 'in': 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'}; then cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(p, json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n', verb='cast', why='<id>: the watchme names its receiver, harbor_master\'s watch verb (39c8d14a459f)') — write(path, text, *, verb, why), text the WHOLE modified ticket. Run it as a script file (a shell command naming a record path and writing is refused by the artifact gate).

D4: green, seal, commit — Run cairn/tools/data_recorder/proofs/test_data_recorder_probes_report_to_the_watch.py (exit 0) and the probe-importing proofs (cairn/tools/data_recorder/proofs/test_reading_declaration.py); each must be green. Seal with `bin/cairn test --seal --timeout 900 cairn/tools/data_recorder/proofs/test_data_recorder_probes_report_to_the_watch.py <the probe-importing proofs>` (it runs each and writes its validation beside it). Commit with message '39c8d14a459f: data_recorder probes report to the watch' (the commit runs the reseal ladder, so allow an hour); commit the commons.

watch_carry is defined in cairn/tools/base/probe.py as watch_carry(ticket_id: str, carry=None, *, fails=None, holds=None) — exactly one of fails=/holds= passed as a keyword. "<its predicate>" is the literal keyword argument named for each file in this decision: fails=_trigger passes that probe module's existing module-level _trigger function (the one already given to Probe(trigger=...)); holds=_holds passes the _holds function this decision says to add. Example: carry=watch_carry(_TICKET_ID, _carry, fails=_trigger).

The proof is created by copying the existing file cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch.py byte for byte (cp), then making ONLY the modifications this ticket lists (docstring, PROVES, BERTH, _REPO_ROOT depth, the three tooth names, plus any tooth this ticket adds). No generator script exists or is used: any earlier mention of child.py names a scratch script of the caster, not something the builder runs. The posts tooth obtains each payload as PROBE.payload({}) — Probe.payload runs the carry over that context.

The receiver is set by ONE Python script file the builder writes in the session scratchpad and runs: for each ticket id it globs the one ticket file, json-loads it, sets spec["receiver"] on every watchme spec whose probe starts with the berth path, and calls cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(path, json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", verb="cast", why=...). A shell command naming a record path while writing is refused by the artifact gate, which is why it is a script file.
